mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and higher discount rates, which in turn depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month does not lead to a statistically significant negative 5-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a positive indicator for the broader economy and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If a sustained increase in HOUST does not lead to a statistically significant positive 60-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5%, it indicates a tight monetary policy, which typically leads to lower S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 4.5% does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in one month signals a supply-side contraction, which is a negative indicator for the economy and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases > 1% in 1 month does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening consumer demand and labor market, which together lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the interaction of RSAFS decreasing and UNRATE increasing does not lead to a statistically significant negative 20-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which is a positive indicator for the broader economy and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If a sustained increase in PAYEMS does not lead to a statistically significant positive 60-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.5% in one month, it signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.5% in 1 month does not lead to a statistically significant positive 5-day forward return on S&P 500 (t-test p > 0.05).
